mn22:0.2: The Simile of the Water Snake
mn22:1.2: At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
mn22:2.1: Now at that time, a monk named Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, had given rise to this harmful wrong view:
mn22:2.2: “As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.”
mn22:2.4: “It is said that the monk named Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, has given rise to this harmful wrong view:
mn22:2.5: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.’”
mn22:3.1: Then those monks approached the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer; having approached, they said to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer:
mn22:3.2: “Is it true, friend Ariṭṭha, that such a harmful wrong view has arisen in you:
mn22:3.3: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them’?”
mn22:3.4: “Indeed, friends, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One thus: those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.”
mn22:3.5: Then those monks, desiring to dissuade the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, from that harmful wrong view, questioned him, cross-examined him, and admonished him:
mn22:3.6: “Do not say so, friend Ariṭṭha; do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One, for the Blessed One would not say such a thing.
mn22:3.7: In many ways, friend Ariṭṭha, obstructive things have been declared obstructive by the Blessed One, and they are sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.
mn22:3.8: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be of little satisfaction, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.
mn22:3.9: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a skeleton …
mn22:3.10: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a piece of meat …
mn22:3.11: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a torch of grass …
mn22:3.12: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a pit of burning coals …
mn22:3.13: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a dream …
mn22:3.14: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like something borrowed …
mn22:3.15: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like the fruit of a tree …
mn22:3.16: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a slaughterhouse …
mn22:3.17: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a sword or spear …
mn22:3.18: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a snake’s head, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.”
mn22:3.19: Yet even so, the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, when questioned, cross-examined, and admonished by those monks, stubbornly clung to and persisted in that harmful wrong view, saying:
mn22:3.20: “Indeed, friends, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One thus: those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.”
mn22:3.21: When those monks were unable to dissuade the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, from that harmful wrong view, they approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat to one side. Sitting to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One:
mn22:3.22: “Venerable sir, a harmful wrong view has arisen in the monk named Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer:
mn22:3.23: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.’
mn22:3.25: ‘It is said that the monk named Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, has given rise to this harmful wrong view—
mn22:3.26: As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.’
mn22:3.27: Then we, venerable sir, approached the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer; having approached, we said to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer:
mn22:3.28: ‘Is it true, friend Ariṭṭha, that such a harmful wrong view has arisen in you—
mn22:3.29: As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them’?”
mn22:3.30: When this was said, venerable sir, the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, said to us:
mn22:3.31: ‘Indeed, friends, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One thus: those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.’
mn22:3.32: Then we, venerable sir, desiring to dissuade the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, from that harmful wrong view, questioned him, cross-examined him, and admonished him:
mn22:3.33: ‘Do not say so, friend Ariṭṭha; do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One, for the Blessed One would not say such a thing.
mn22:3.34: In many ways, friend Ariṭṭha, obstructive things have been declared obstructive by the Blessed One, and they are sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.
mn22:3.35: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be of little satisfaction, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.
mn22:3.36: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a skeleton …
mn22:3.37: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a snake’s head, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.’
mn22:3.38: Yet even so, venerable sir, the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, when questioned, cross-examined, and admonished by us, stubbornly clung to and persisted in that harmful wrong view, saying:
mn22:3.39: ‘Indeed, friends, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One thus: those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.’
mn22:4.1: When we, venerable sir, were unable to dissuade the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, from that harmful wrong view, we came to report this matter to the Blessed One.”
mn22:5.1: Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk:
mn22:5.2: “Go, monk, and in my name summon the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, saying:
mn22:5.4: “Yes, venerable sir,” that monk replied to the Blessed One and approached the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer; having approached, he said to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer:
mn22:5.6: “Yes, friend,” replied the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, to that monk, and he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat to one side. Sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer:
mn22:5.7: “Is it true, Ariṭṭha, that such a harmful wrong view has arisen in you:
mn22:5.8: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them’?”
mn22:5.9: “Indeed, venerable sir, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One thus: ‘those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.’”
mn22:6.1: “To whom, foolish man, do you understand that I have taught the Dhamma in this way?
mn22:6.2: Have I not, foolish man, declared in many ways that obstructive things are obstructive, and they are sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them?
mn22:6.3: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be of little satisfaction, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.
mn22:6.4: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a skeleton …
mn22:6.5: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a piece of meat …
mn22:6.6: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a torch of grass …
mn22:6.7: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a pit of burning coals …
mn22:6.8: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a dream …
mn22:6.9: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like something borrowed …
mn22:6.10: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like the fruit of a tree …
mn22:6.11: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a slaughterhouse …
mn22:6.12: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a sword or spear …
mn22:6.13: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a snake’s head, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.
mn22:6.14: Yet you, foolish man, by your wrong grasp of the teaching, misrepresent us, harm yourself, and generate much demerit.
mn22:6.15: This, foolish man, will lead to your harm and suffering for a long time.”
mn22:7.1: Then the Blessed One addressed the monks:
mn22:7.3: Has this monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, even kindled a spark of understanding in this Dhamma and Discipline?”
mn22:7.6: When this was said, the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, sat silent, dismayed, with shoulders slumped, head down, brooding, and unable to respond.
mn22:7.7: Then the Blessed One, seeing the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, silent, dismayed, with shoulders slumped, head down, brooding, and unable to respond, said to him:
mn22:7.8: “You, foolish man, will be recognized by your own harmful wrong view.
mn22:7.9: Here, I will question the monks.”
mn22:8.1: Then the Blessed One addressed the monks:
mn22:8.2: “Do you too, monks, understand the Dhamma taught by me as this monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, understands it, who by his wrong grasp misrepresents us, harms himself, and generates much demerit?”
mn22:8.4: For in many ways, venerable sir, obstructive things have been declared obstructive by the Blessed One, and they are sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.
mn22:8.5: They are sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.
mn22:8.6: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be of little satisfaction, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.
mn22:8.7: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a skeleton …
mn22:8.8: Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be like a snake’s head, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.”
mn22:8.9: “Good, good, monks! It is good that you understand the Dhamma taught by me thus.
mn22:8.10: For in many ways, monks, I have declared obstructive things to be obstructive, and they are sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.
mn22:8.11: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be of little satisfaction, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.
mn22:8.12: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a skeleton …
mn22:8.13: Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a snake’s head, full of suffering, full of trouble, with even greater danger herein.
mn22:8.14: Yet this monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, by his wrong grasp misrepresents us, harms himself, and generates much demerit.
mn22:8.15: This, for that foolish man, will lead to his harm and suffering for a long time.
